reason: Date A wins the numerical tie with B through fewer controls and better action visibility at 200%; B offers clearer segmented entry. Answer C makes the question the strongest element without losing the primary action at 200%; A is preferable for immediate access to Back. Neither winner reaches the authorized A>=9 and F>=9 threshold across screen and components.
limitations: Scores combine normal and 200% evidence. Component vectors use the same six dimensions as screen scores. Null means passive-component feedback is inapplicable or baseline interaction feedback is unobservable; remaining dimensions are normalized.

Only the supplied screenshots and the two permitted files were inspected. checks.json records no overflow for all 12 alternative/size combinations; it contains no detailed action/result, focus, contrast or error-state observations.

Prototype source establishes implemented rules, not independently observed runtime outcomes. Feedback scores assess limited study behavior; submission, validation, storage, inference and real Back navigation receive no credit.
The baseline runtime, contrast and reduced-motion evidence described by the user is acknowledged, but does not establish specific input validation, recovery, keyboard or screen-reader outcomes.

Offscreen controls are not treated as inaccessible merely because scrolling is required. No production-task hard-gate failure is established by these composition studies; the prototypes cannot be accepted as completed production flows.
Physical/native and assistive-technology proof remains separate and unverified. No blanket score reduction was applied for that deferred boundary, and no full/native 9/10 certification is made.
